To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) IL-2 signaling prevents the expression of genes that induce T cell unresponsiveness; (b) the IL-2 signaling pathway that inhibits the expression of nergic genes is mTOR-dependent; (c) the IL- 2-induced mTOR activation leads to the induction of a set of transcription factors that inhibit the expression of nergizing genes.
IL-2 signaling inhibits anergy through mTORC2-dependent activation of NFAT.
L-2 signaling inhibits the expression of genes encoding nergy-inducing proteins by activating the mTOR pathway.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of genes that are involved in the regulation of T cell responses.
the molecular and cellular basis for T cell activation and tolerance.
the identification of the molecular mechanisms by which the IL-2 signaling pathway prevents T cell an energy and how these mechanisms are regulated.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the IL-2 signaling pathway plays a central role in the regulation of T cell fate by controlling the expression of anergizing genes and the activity of mTOR.
the L-2 signaling prevents the expression of anergy-inducing genes and promotes the expression of anti-anergic genes, which in turn prevent T cell anergy.
IL-2 is a potent anti- anergizing cytokine that can prevent anergy through the activation of mTOR, which is essential for the expression of genes that promote T cell activation and proliferation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IL-2 signaling prevents energy by inhibiting the energy-inducing genes and by activating mTOR, which in turn promotes the expression of genes that prevent anergy.
IL-2 signaling inhibits the expression of genes that induce T cell anergy.
IL-2 signaling prevents the induction of anergy by activating mTOR, which, in turn, prevents the induction of a specific program that is required for the establishment of anergy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the IL-2/IL-2R pathway plays a critical role in preventing T cell energy.
the mTOR pathway is required for the reversal of T cell anergy and that this is due to the regulation of the expression of the anergy-inducing genes by mTOR.
IL-2 signaling prevents anergy by inhibitting the expression of nnergy-inducing genes.
